objective.text: Find partners to ten and describe a teen number as ten and some ones.

source_ref.section: L1 lesson content in the combined Module 1 concept JSON; objective adapted from its explanations and questions

explanations.title: L1 Ten-frame: 9 and 1 make 10
explanations.text: A ten-frame has 10 spots. Here 9 spots are full. Only 1 spot is empty. So 9 plus 1 equals 10. Also, 10 minus 1 equals 9. And 10 minus 9 equals 1.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Ten-Frame Flash

explanations.title: L1 Number bond to 10
explanations.text: A number bond shows a total and two parts. The total is the big number. Here the total is 10. If one part is 5, the other part is 5. So 5 plus 5 equals 10.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Pairs to Ten with Number Bonds

explanations.title: L1 Say Ten way
explanations.text: Some people say numbers the Say Ten way. You say the ten first, then the ones. 13 is said ten 3. Ten 3 means 10 plus 3. So 10 plus 3 equals 13.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Happy Counting the Say Ten Way

explanations.title: L1 Add a ten and some ones
explanations.text: When you add 10 and some ones, the answer has a ten and those ones. Look at ten 5. It means 10 plus 5. So 10 plus 5 equals 15.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Say Ten as Ten Plus Facts

misconceptions.label: Mixing up fourteen and forty
misconceptions.description: The English word fourteen puts the ones before the ten, so a child can confuse a teen number with a tens number such as forty.
detection_signals: Child says 'forty' or answers 40 when fourteen (or 10 plus 4) is expected.
Child answers a tens number such as 40 for a teen-number sum.
misconceptions.response_text: Careful, fourteen is not forty. Fourteen is said ten 4. It means 10 plus 4.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Happy Counting the Say Ten Way (note: fourteen is easily confused with forty)
